nodes.name: Gmail Trigger
nodes.notes: Poll the test inbox once a minute. Simplify is off so the body is included. Use a Gmail credential whose only scope is https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly. Do not grant compose, modify, or send scopes, and do not add a Gmail send node.

nodes.name: Manual sample email
nodes.notes: Editor-only sample. It does not poll Gmail and it does not send mail.

nodes.name: Load sample email
nodes.notes: Provide one synthetic message in the same shape the Gmail trigger emits.

nodes.name: Normalize email
nodes.notes: Turn the Gmail message into the API fields. Skip drafts, sent mail, empty messages, and messages without a body.

nodes.name: Email is usable
nodes.notes: True when the normalizer produced an API payload.

nodes.name: Call Python API
nodes.notes: POST the normalized email. On this computer the API is http://127.0.0.1:8000. If n8n runs in Docker, change the host to host.docker.internal and set APP_HOST=0.0.0.0. Attach a Header Auth credential named X-API-Key. Do not type the key into this node. The timeout covers classification and one reply retry. This node does not send email.

nodes.name: API call succeeded
nodes.notes: HTTP 201 is a new result. HTTP 200 is an existing result.

nodes.name: Email already processed
nodes.notes: The API kept the original row and did not call the model again.

nodes.name: Needs human priority review
nodes.notes: Route only the priority returned by the API. Do not classify the email again.

nodes.name: Route error type
nodes.notes: Separate credential, model, database, and validation failures. The fallback is any other workflow error.

nodes.name: Record skipped email
nodes.notes: Store the outcome in the n8n execution. This does not send email or an external notification.

nodes.name: Record duplicate
nodes.notes: Store the outcome in the n8n execution. This does not send email or an external notification.
